sectionsContent.title: Molecular Geometry

concept.summary: Count on the central atom only. A single, double or triple bond each counts as one bonding pair.
keyIdeas: Electron groups = bonding pairs + lone pairs. Use your PhET sheet or the Common Molecular Shapes table (slide 19) to name the shape and give the bond angle.

sectionsContent.directions: For each compound, add up the valence electrons and show the addition. Draw the Lewis structure with every lone pair. Then fill in the bonding pairs and lone pairs on the central atom, the shape name and the bond angle. We will do number 1 together.

headers: Lewis structure (reminder: extra electrons form lone pairs; not enough means extra bonds)

keyNotes: Number 1 (CH₄) is the example you complete with the class. It is blank on the student copy and not scored; the 10 points are rows 2–11.

Bonding pairs are counted the way slide 17 counts electron groups: a single, double or triple bond to the central atom is one. A student who writes 4 for CS₂ counted shared pairs; send them back to the Remember box. Lone pairs are counted on the central atom only.
CHCl₃: C has 4 bonds (1 H, 3 Cl) and no lone pairs; each Cl carries 3 lone pairs (18 + 8 = 26). COCl₂: C=O plus two C–Cl (24). CS₂: two C=S (16).
Octet exception: PCl₅. P has 5 bonds, so 10 electrons. P is in period 3 and can hold more than 8; C, N, O and F cannot (slide 18).

SO₂: the key shows the octet-rule form, one S=O and one S–O. Accept the double bond on either side, and O=S=O with one lone pair on S: S still has 3 electron groups and 1 lone pair, so shape and angle are the same.
Slide 19 gives about 107° and about 104.5°; students will copy those for PCl₃ and OF₂. Accept them or any answer under 109.5°. Measured: PCl₃ about 100°, OF₂ about 103°, SO₂ about 119°.
SO₂ (bent from 3 groups) and PCl₅ (trigonal bipyramidal) come from the PhET Molecule Shapes activity, which students do first.
